data.gender_notes: Rivkah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘rivka’ which means ‘to see’ or ‘to be seen’. In the Old Testament, Rivkah is the name of the wife of Isaac and the mother of Jacob and Esau. She is a woman of deep faith who was chosen by God to fulfill a divine promise. The name Rivkah carries the meaning “God's promise” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rivkah usually hope their child will grow to embody god's promise and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Rivkah’s name holds significant cultural importance in Jewish and Christian traditions. In Jewish tradition, Rivkah is revered as the matriarch of the Jewish people and her story is celebrated during the holiday of Rosh Hashanah. In Christian tradition, Rivkah is a key figure in the Old Testament, and her story serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness and promise-keeping abilities.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, Rivkah represents faithfulness and obedience to God's will. She was obedient to God's call to marry Isaac, despite the difficulties and challenges that came with it. Her story also highlights God's sovereignty and his ability to use even seemingly insignificant events to fulfill his larger plan. Additionally, the name Rivkah can serve as a reminder to see and acknowledge the supporting roles that God uses to fulfill his larger purposes.
